title: Model-id schema pattern cannot express Workers AI ids (@cf/...)
description:
Blocks routing the cloud orchestrator at Workers AI, which the design names as a first-class provider rung and which this factory is configured for.

Every Workers AI model id begins with @ — for example @cf/openai/gpt-oss-120b, confirmed live against the operator account. The qualified form the entrypoint expects is therefore workers-ai/@cf/openai/gpt-oss-120b. The schema pattern rejects it:

  orchestrator.model: workers-ai/@cf/openai/gpt-oss-120b does not match
  ^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9_.+-]*(/[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9_.+-]*)*$

So a factory configured for Workers AI cannot name a Workers AI model. The pattern was written for vendor/model shapes and never met an id with a namespace sigil.

Fix the pattern in ALL THREE implementations that validate it — skills/ticks/references/runners-config.schema.json, the Go loader, and the Python reference validator — so they cannot drift; 728 established that these three must agree. Allow @ only where Workers AI actually puts it (leading a path segment), not anywhere in the string, so the pattern stays a real constraint rather than becoming permissive.

Add a test case per implementation using a REAL Workers AI id, and keep a negative case proving genuinely malformed ids still fail. Note runners-config.md documents the model grammar — update it in the same change.
